setting: The open feather-grass steppe south of Kaniv on the Dnipro frontier, late summer 1628, at sunset and dusk: rolling plain, ancient Scythian burial mounds (kurgans) with weathered stone idols, wooden signal beacon towers ('figury') that are set alight to warn of raids, shallow ravines (balky), oak groves, swarms of hares fleeing locust-stricken lands. A light Cossack patrol armed only with bows, sabres, spears and lassos (no firearms) ambushes a small Tatar raiding party driving twelve Ukrainian captives toward the Dnipro crossing. Later scenes: the night ride home under the Milky Way (the 'Chumak Way'), the timber castle and town of Kaniv on green hills above the Dnipro, graves of the fallen on the high Dnipro bank (the hill where Shevchenko's grave will later stand). One epilogue image is set at Zhovti Vody, May 1648.

characters.ivan: Ivan, a tall lean 42-year-old Cossack otaman with a weathered hawk-nosed face, deep-set grey eyes, chestnut forelock, long dark mustache streaked with grey, dark-blue zhupan, green sash, red sharovary, composite bow and quiver, sabre
characters.sokil: Sokil, a slender keen-eyed 22-year-old Cossack scout with a narrow young face, light-brown forelock, thin fair mustache, grey sheepskin kalpak, ochre zhupan, blue sharovary, composite bow
characters.hlukhyi: Hlukhyi, a thickset 35-year-old Cossack with a short black forelock, thick black mustache, a notched right ear, grey-brown wool svyta, black sharovary, long spear and sabre
characters.hladkyi: Hladkyi, a big heavy 45-year-old Cossack with round cheeks, brown drooping mustache, red-topped fur kalpak, brown zhupan, dark-green sharovary, sabre
characters.jalai: Jalai, a lean hard 35-year-old Crimean Tatar raid leader with high cheekbones, narrow dark eyes, sparse black beard, fox-fur cap, quilted brown kaftan, withered left arm held stiffly, composite bow, riding a dun steppe horse
characters.tatar_raiders: Crimean Tatar horsemen in quilted brown and ochre kaftans and sheepskin caps, composite bows, sabres, lassos, small shaggy steppe horses
characters.captives: Ukrainian village captives: men in linen shirts and grey svytas, women in embroidered white shirts, dark skirts and white headscarves, a few children, wrists bound with rope
characters.kaniv_merchants: Jewish merchants of Kaniv, bearded middle-aged men in long dark kaftans and fur hats, calm and businesslike
characters.pidstarosta: the pidstarosta of Kaniv, a 55-year-old Ruthenian nobleman with a grey mustache, shaved temples, fur-trimmed crimson kontusz and sabre

palette: Warm sunset gold, red and long violet dusk over pale straw-colored feather grass; dust hanging in low sun; deep blue starlit night with the Milky Way; soft green-grey mornings over the Dnipro at Kaniv. Cossack clothes blue, ochre, red, grey; Tatars in brown, ochre and sheepskin.
notes: The source text is very violent (arrow wounds, dismemberment, torture); images show only implied violence: drawn bows, arrows in flight, raised sabres, lassos, riders falling in dust, still figures seen from behind or covered. Sokil's death is shown with dignity (still form in the grass, face turned away; later a wrapped body on a horse, a grave). Cossacks carry no firearms in this story. Jewish merchants must be depicted respectfully and naturally, as period townspeople. Ivan's hand wound exists only in branch r.0.0. In the 1648 epilogue Ivan is about 62 and Jalai about 55, now allies.
